reason: The text presents God's compassionate response to His people's suffering as the basis for His leadership and action to deliver them. The passage emphasizes that God 'has surely seen the affliction' of His people, 'has heard their cry,' and 'knows their sorrows' (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה רָאֹ֥ה רָאִ֛יתִי אֶת־ עֳנִ֥י עַמִּ֖י...וְאֶת־ צַעֲקָתָ֤ם שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי...כִּ֥י יָדַ֖עְתִּי אֶת־ מַכְאֹבָֽיו). This empathetic understanding directly motivates God's redemptive action ('I have come down to deliver them'). The passage thus models good leadership through compassion—understanding and responding to the suffering of those being led.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
